# Pharos

> Pharos tracks 396 active stablecoins across major chains with depeg alerts, liquidity scores, on-chain safety signals, dependency-risk scoring, and report-card-style risk summaries. Data refreshes multiple times per day from the Pharos Cloudflare Worker API.

## Core Data

- [Dashboard homepage](https://pharos.watch/): Market overview with KPI bar, peg-score heatmap, and stablecoin list.
- [Safety Scores](https://pharos.watch/safety-scores/): Safety Score V10 three-pillar Backing / Exit / Economic Control model with evidence-backed grades from A+ to F.
- [Pharos Stability Index](https://pharos.watch/stability-index/): Aggregate market-stability gauge with history chart.
- [DEWS (Depeg Early Warning System)](https://pharos.watch/depeg/): Active depegs, watch-list, and historical DEWS bands.
- [Liquidity](https://pharos.watch/liquidity/): DEX liquidity scores, pool counts, TVL depth.
- [Yield](https://pharos.watch/yield/): Yield-bearing stablecoin intelligence.
- [Non-USD Market Structure](https://pharos.watch/alt-pegs/): Historical and current market structure for non-USD stablecoin cohorts.
- [Chains](https://pharos.watch/chains/): Per-chain stablecoin distribution and health.
- [Flows](https://pharos.watch/flows/): Mint/burn flow dashboards.
- [FreezeWatch](https://pharos.watch/freezewatch/): Issuer freeze events and exposure.
- [Dependency Map](https://pharos.watch/dependency-map/): Inter-stablecoin dependency graph.
- [Coverage](https://pharos.watch/coverage/): What Pharos tracks and what it does not.
- [Cemetery](https://pharos.watch/cemetery/): 113 defunct stablecoins and their causes of death.
- [Stablecoin Cemetery dataset (JSON)](https://pharos.watch/datasets/stablecoin-cemetery.json): Citation-ready dataset of failed, discontinued, and abandoned stablecoins.
- [Stablecoin Cemetery dataset (CSV)](https://pharos.watch/datasets/stablecoin-cemetery.csv): Tabular export of the Stablecoin Cemetery dataset.
- [Upcoming](https://pharos.watch/upcoming/): Pre-launch stablecoins Pharos is tracking.

## Methodology

- [Methodology Hub](https://pharos.watch/methodology/): Scoring methods for safety, peg, liquidity and yield; dependency limits through V10 parent and backing relationships, not a contagion simulator.
- [Safety Scores Changelog](https://pharos.watch/methodology/scoring-changelog/): Every weight change since v1.0.
- [Depeg + DEWS Changelog](https://pharos.watch/methodology/depeg-changelog/): Peg-deviation detection and early-warning stress methodology history.
- [Depeg Duration Resolver Changelog](https://pharos.watch/methodology/depeg-resolver-changelog/): Forecasting, resolution, and review methodology history for confirmed depeg incidents.
- [Liquidity Score Changelog](https://pharos.watch/methodology/liquidity-score-changelog/): DEX market-depth, confidence, and coverage methodology history.
- [Redemption Backstop Changelog](https://pharos.watch/methodology/redemption-backstop-changelog/): Standalone redemption-route scoring history and V9 Exit evidence evolution.
- [Stability Index Changelog](https://pharos.watch/methodology/stability-index-changelog/): System-wide stablecoin stability index methodology history.
- [Chain Health Changelog](https://pharos.watch/methodology/chain-health-changelog/): Chain Health factor, evidence, and rating methodology history.
- [Yield Intelligence Changelog](https://pharos.watch/methodology/yield-changelog/): Yield sourcing, risk, scoring, and publication methodology history.
- [Blacklist Tracker Changelog](https://pharos.watch/methodology/blacklist-tracker-changelog/): Address monitoring, event normalization, and coverage methodology history.
- [Mint/Burn Flow Changelog](https://pharos.watch/methodology/mint-burn-flow-changelog/): Issuance-flow detection, scoring, and publication methodology history.
- [Pricing Pipeline Changelog](https://pharos.watch/methodology/pricing-pipeline-changelog/): Price-source selection, consensus, validation, and fallback methodology history.

## Learn

- [Stablecoin Definitions](https://pharos.watch/methodology/#definitions): 41 citation-ready definitions for Pharos stablecoin analytics terminology.
- [Definition: PSI (Pharos Stability Index)](https://pharos.watch/methodology/#def-psi): An ecosystem-wide condition score from 0 to 100, recomputed every 30 minutes. It subtracts penalties for active depeg severity, depeg breadth, and DEWS stress breadth, then adds a bounded market-cap trend term. The result maps into 6 condition bands from BEDROCK to MELTDOWN. PSI is conservative by design: one small depeg should not move the index, but broad simultaneous stress should.
- [Definition: DEWS (Depeg Early Warning System)](https://pharos.watch/methodology/#def-dews): A forward-looking per-coin stress score from 0 to 100, recomputed every 30 minutes from 8 weighted sub-signals: Supply Velocity, Pool Balance Drift, Liquidity Erosion, Price Confidence, Cross-Source Divergence, Blacklist Activity, Mint/Burn Flow, Yield Anomaly. Weak PSI and same-peg contagion can amplify the score before it lands in a band. It is a normalized stress score, not a calibrated probability.
- [Definition: Peg Score](https://pharos.watch/methodology/#def-peg-score): A 0-100 score for a stablecoin's historical peg behavior, combining time-at-peg (50%) and event severity (50%), minus penalties for active depegs and erratic behavior. It needs at least 7 days of tracking; scores under 30 days are marked early. NAV tokens return NR because they are not meant to hold a fixed price. Peg Score enters the Safety Score as a multiplier.
- [Definition: Safety Score](https://pharos.watch/methodology/#def-safety-score): Pharos's V10 risk grade for a stablecoin. It evaluates Backing (40%), Exit (35%), and Economic Control (25%) with bounded aggregation, so a strong pillar cannot average away a weak material path. Peg behavior, dependencies, wrappers, evidence quality, track record, and structural caps can then only constrain the result. Grades run from A+ (87+) to F (below 40); NR means required evidence is insufficient.
- [Definition: Liquidity Score](https://pharos.watch/methodology/#def-liquidity-score): A 0-100 score for how easily a stablecoin can be exited through DEX markets, combining TVL Depth (30%), Volume (20%), Pool Quality (20%), Durability (20%), Diversity (10%). Thin, stale, or identity-poor pools stay visible for diagnostics but receive no scoring weight. It is an aggregate market score, not a single-route execution test.
- [Definition: DDR (Depeg Duration Resolver)](https://pharos.watch/methodology/#def-ddr): For each confirmed depeg incident, DDR publishes a Resolution Outlook (Recovery Likely, At Risk, Recovery Unlikely, or Insufficient Signal) from transparent mechanistic rules and, when recovery is plausible, an Expected Duration band drawn from Pharos's corpus of recovered depegs. Each incident gets one immutable prediction, sealed at forecast readiness or the 72-hour backstop. It is a structural read, not a probability or investment advice.
- [Stablecoin Mechanisms](https://pharos.watch/learn/mechanisms/): 10 plain-English explainers for the stablecoin mechanism archetypes Pharos tracks.
- [Mechanism: Cash and Treasuries, tokenized 1:1](https://pharos.watch/learn/mechanisms/fiat-cash/): Centralized issuers custody dollars in bank accounts and short-term Treasuries; tokens are minted and redeemed on demand.
- [Mechanism: Treasury-backed tokens: rising NAV or stable $1 units](https://pharos.watch/learn/mechanisms/tbill/): Short-duration Treasuries support two families: NAV-accreting tokens and par-stable $1 tokens with separately distributed or retained yield.
- [Mechanism: Mint debt against crypto collateral](https://pharos.watch/learn/mechanisms/cdp/): Overcollateralized vaults issue stablecoin debt; positions liquidate when collateral falls below a safety ratio.
- [Mechanism: Offsetting exposures, strategy-dependent carry](https://pharos.watch/learn/mechanisms/synthetic-delta-neutral/): Delta neutrality can pair spot crypto with short perpetuals or pair borrowed native assets with matched staked exposure; the yield and failure modes depend on the variant.
- [Mechanism: Programmatic peg defense, with different collateral models](https://pharos.watch/learn/mechanisms/algorithmic/): Protocol-level supply rules and arbitrage defend the peg; current designs can hold real collateral, unlike historical pure mint/burn systems.
- [Mechanism: Tokenize a private credit fund share](https://pharos.watch/learn/mechanisms/rwa-credit-fund/): Regulated funds hold private credit, CLO tranches, or other non-Treasury debt; the token is a fund share whose NAV reflects credit losses and quarterly redemption gates.
- [Mechanism: A title claim on specific vaulted metal](https://pharos.watch/learn/mechanisms/commodity-claim/): The token is not a dollar claim. It is legal title to identified bars of gold or silver sitting in a named vault, usually redeemable for physical delivery in whole-bar lots.
- [Mechanism: Own a fund share, not a cash reserve claim](https://pharos.watch/learn/mechanisms/ucits-trs-fund/): Physical securities and total-return swaps can target a cash-like return without turning the portfolio into Treasury bills.
- [Mechanism: Several liabilities, one shared reserve](https://pharos.watch/learn/mechanisms/shared-reserve/): Protocol exchange access is an operational claim, not proof that each token owns an exclusive slice of the pool.
- [Mechanism: A protocol claim on positions, not direct cash ownership](https://pharos.watch/learn/mechanisms/protocol-position/): Bridge, vault and module liabilities retain local accounting, custody and recovery risk even when the underlying asset is a stablecoin.
- [Stablecoin Case Studies](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/): 27 long-form retrospectives on stablecoin depegs, failures, and recoveries.
- [Case study: USDC and the Silicon Valley Bank weekend](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/usdc-svb-2023/): A fully-reserved dollar stablecoin lost its peg for two days in March 2023, not because its backing failed, but because one of the banks holding that backing did.
- [Case study: LUSD: the peg that held during the SVB weekend](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/lusd-flight-to-safety-2023/): While USDC, Dai, and FRAX broke below $0.90 in March 2023, LUSD, backed only by on-chain ETH and an arbitrage-enforced redemption floor, traded at a premium and repegged in under 15 hours.
- [Case study: TerraUSD: the death spiral that erased $18 billion](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/terra-ust-2022/): An uncollateralized mint-burn stablecoin propped up by a 20% yield unwound in six days, hyperinflating LUNA and dragging UST to a dime.
- [Case study: Dai: Black Thursday and the PSM dependency](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/dai-black-thursday/): A crypto-collateralized stablecoin that survived two very different shocks (broken liquidations in 2020 and inherited reserve risk in 2023) and was reshaped by each.
- [Case study: USDe and the October 2025 Binance oracle print](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/usde-oracle-2025/): During the 10 October 2025 crypto-wide deleveraging, USDe printed as low as ~$0.65 on Binance while its backing and primary-market redemption stayed intact: a venue artifact, not a peg break.
- [Case study: BUIDL: the tokenized T-bill that held](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/buidl-tokenized-tbill-2025/): BlackRock's BUIDL did the unglamorous thing a tokenized money-market fund is supposed to do: hold NAV, constrain access, disclose its structure, and become safer precisely because it was not pretending to be an ungated retail dollar.
- [Case study: USYC: when a T-bill fund became DeFi collateral](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/usyc-nav-pricing-2025/): USYC's Treasury portfolio did not fail. The wound was downstream: protocols treated a permissioned NAV fund share like instantly liquid stablecoin collateral, then learned that NAV, market price, and redemption access are different things.
- [Case study: USD0++ depeg: when Usual changed the redemption floor](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/usd0pp-usual-2025/): A governance decision, not a backing failure, repriced Usual's locked USD0++ to roughly 89 cents and set off a deleveraging cascade across Morpho.
- [Case study: crvUSD's exploit trilogy: three shocks, no collapse](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/crvusd-exploit-trilogy/): Three exploit-driven stress events across two years each pushed crvUSD off peg by single-digit percentages, and each time it recovered within hours.
- [Case study: sUSD and SIP-420: the depeg a governance vote chose](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/susd-sip420-2025/): Synthetix did not get hacked and did not go insolvent. It voted to pool its debt and drop the collateral ratio (removing the very incentive that had kept sUSD at a dollar), then, a year later, voted to freeze and retire the token outright.
- [Case study: IRON Finance & TITAN: the algorithmic prequel to Terra](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/iron-titan-2021/): A partially collateralized stablecoin whose redemption loop minted its own share token into oblivion: crypto's first large-scale bank run, eleven months before UST.
- [Case study: Neutrino USD: the stablecoin collapse before Terra](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/usdn-neutrino-2022/): A WAVES-collateralized algorithmic stablecoin that broke peg in April 2022 on circular-leverage allegations, never durably recovered, and was quietly retired as the floating index token XTN.
- [Case study: Fei Protocol: the peg that broke at birth](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/fei-protocol/): A $1.3B genesis raise and a reflexive incentive engine could not hold the dollar; after an $80M lending hack, Tribe DAO voted to wind the whole thing down.
- [Case study: Resolv USD: when one key minted eighty million](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/usr-resolv-2026/): USR was a delta-neutral synthetic dollar with an insurance tranche and real-time reserve attestations. None of it mattered once a single privileged key could mint unbacked supply with no cap.
- [Case study: Stream Finance: loss broke three stablecoins](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/stream-elixir-contagion-2025/): A ~$93M off-chain trading loss at Stream Finance detonated a ~$285M cross-protocol cascade, because xUSD had been re-hypothecated as leveraged collateral across lending markets that priced it at a hardcoded $1.
- [Case study: USDf and the opacity discount](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/usdf-falcon-2025/): In July 2025 Falcon's USDf became the first delta-neutral synthetic dollar to be wounded by what holders could not see (opaque off-chain collateral and a seven-day redemption lag) rather than by anything its mechanism actually did wrong.
- [Case study: FDUSD and the insolvency tweet](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/fdusd-sun-fdt-2025/): A fully-reserved dollar stablecoin lost its peg for hours in April 2025, not because its backing failed, but because a high-profile competitor publicly called its custodian insolvent and the market ran first and checked later.
- [Case study: BUSD: the regulator's off-switch](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/busd-paxos-2023/): The third-largest stablecoin did not depeg; it was lawfully wound down. A fully-reserved, solvent coin can still die by order.
- [Case study: Multichain USDC: the bridge died, not the dollar](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/multichain-usdc-2023/): Bridge-wrapped USDC on Fantom fell to roughly $0.22 in July 2023 while real USDC never moved a basis point: the backing lived on a bridge that one arrested founder controlled outright.
- [Case study: The FTX weekend: which pegs broke](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/ftx-contagion-2022/): When the second-largest crypto exchange collapsed in November 2022, the stablecoins that wobbled were not the weakest by design but the ones standing closest to Alameda's order flow.
- [Case study: USDR: tokenized houses cannot sell at 3 AM](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/usdr-real-usd-2023/): Tangible's Real USD was backed by real assets, but not liquid ones. When the DAI cushion drained, holders discovered that on-chain redemptions move in seconds and real estate does not.
- [Case study: Euro Tether: the stablecoin that died by jurisdiction](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/eurt-mica-exit-2024/): EURT never broke its euro peg. In November 2024 Tether simply withdrew it rather than pursue MiCA authorization: the first wave of EU rules retired a non-dollar stablecoin instead of cracking it.
- [Case study: USDD: when the issuer pulled the Bitcoin](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/usdd-tron-reserve-2024/): No dramatic depeg. The shock was structural: the TRON DAO Reserve quietly withdrew ~12,000 BTC, leaving USDD backed almost entirely by TRX, before a 2025 redesign into an overcollateralized CDP.
- [Case study: Kava USDX: one toxic collateral leg](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/usdx-kava-2022/): An overcollateralized CDP dollar broke its peg in May 2022 because a single whitelisted collateral asset, TerraUSD, collapsed, and it never durably recovered.
- [Case study: MAI: the bridge that broke the peg](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/mai-qidao-bridge-2023/): QiDao's overcollateralized stablecoin lost its dollar in 2023, not because its collateral fell, but because the Multichain bridge collapse stranded the assets backing the MAI minted on Fantom and seeded bad debt that the multichain footprint propagated.
- [Case study: pmUSD and the in-situ gold collateral chain](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/pmusd-precious-metals/): RAAC's gold-RWA dollar token has never settled at par (hundreds of recorded sub-peg events, then an ~88% crater to its May 4, 2026 all-time low), yet it is still live. The story is structural, not a single blowup.
- [Case study: apxUSD and the Bitcoin-treasury collateral chain](https://pharos.watch/learn/case-studies/apxusd-dat-collateral/): Apyx markets apxUSD as an RWA-backed dollar, but roughly 62% of its reserve is Strategy preferred equity, a Bitcoin-correlated asset that fell with crypto in early June 2026, opening a downside depeg that is still unresolved.

## API

- [API Access](https://pharos.watch/api/): Supporter keys for donors and partner keys on request; free Safety Score grades without a key.
- [API Reference](https://pharos.watch/api/#reference): Public and ops lanes, auth model, response contracts, and every public endpoint.
- [OpenAPI spec](https://pharos.watch/openapi.json): Machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 endpoint catalogue for the Pharos API.
- [Postman collection](https://pharos.watch/postman/pharos-api.postman_collection.json): Importable Pharos API collection for external integrations.
- [Postman environment](https://pharos.watch/postman/pharos-api.postman_environment.json): Production environment template with API key placeholder.
- [Funding](https://pharos.watch/funding/): Public ledger of Pharos running costs, donations, and sustainability path.
- [About](https://pharos.watch/about/): Project context and data sources.

## Docs

- [Documentation Archive](https://pharos.watch/docs/): Methodology and API reference documentation.
- [Classification](https://pharos.watch/docs/classification/): Stablecoin classification methodology for peg currencies, backing models, governance labels, commodity pegs, lifecycle status, and taxonomy pages.
- [Stablecoin Listing Policy](https://pharos.watch/docs/listing-policy/): How Pharos admits, classifies, quarantines, delists, and preserves stablecoin records while separating catalog policy from runtime pricing failures.
- [Pricing Pipeline](https://pharos.watch/docs/pricing-pipeline/): How Pharos computes stablecoin prices: source consensus, peg-aware validation, fallback enrichment, stale-data handling, and override policy.
- [Depeg Detection](https://pharos.watch/docs/depeg-detection/): Depeg detection methodology covering two-stage confirmation, peg-score inputs, severity bands, event lifecycle, and recovery handling.
- [DEWS](https://pharos.watch/docs/dews/): Depeg Early Warning System methodology: DEWS formula, stress sub-signals, bands, downgrade gates, and API response contract.
- [DEX Liquidity](https://pharos.watch/docs/dex-liquidity/): DEX Liquidity Score methodology for stablecoins: pool discovery, depth scoring, durability, pair diversity, cross-validation, and risk bands.
- [Pharos Stability Index](https://pharos.watch/docs/stability-index/): Pharos Stability Index methodology explaining the PSI formula, active universe, stress bands, storage model, API surface, and replay rules.
- [Report Cards](https://pharos.watch/docs/report-cards/): Stablecoin V9 report-card methodology for Backing, Exit, Economic Control, peg behavior, dependency exposure, evidence constraints, and portfolios.
- [Redemption Backstops](https://pharos.watch/docs/redemption-backstops/): Redemption Backstops methodology for standalone route scoring, redemption terms, V9 Exit evidence, operational disclosures, and stored review evidence.
- [Chain Health](https://pharos.watch/docs/chain-health/): Chain Health Score methodology for stablecoin networks: supply concentration, venue health, deployment coverage, risk factors, and score bands.
- [Mint Burn Flows](https://pharos.watch/docs/mint-burn-flows/): Mint and burn flow methodology covering issuance-chain ingestion, pressure scoring, Bank Run Gauge inputs, reconciliation, and backfills.
- [Yield Intelligence](https://pharos.watch/docs/yield-intelligence/): Yield Intelligence methodology for stablecoin APY resolution, Pharos Yield Score, source confidence, reward warnings, and risk-adjusted ranking.
- [PSI Historical Assets](https://pharos.watch/docs/shadow-stablecoins/): Off-catalog PSI historical assets: authoritative continuity, monitoring eligibility, public listing exclusions and unavailable source history.

Docs support `Accept: text/markdown` content negotiation for agent consumption.

## Digest

- [USD1 Leads A Split Flow Tape](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-17/): USD1 net burned $14.39M at a -100 pressure reading while USDat minted a net $4.45M at +100. The Bank Run Gauge sits at -8; a print of -15 or lower would move flow stress to the front.
- [USDT Sheds $824M In A Week](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-16/): USDT supply fell $824.16M in seven days, under half a percent of its float, while USDA (alpha partner) widened to 264 bps from 89. Next trigger: a $45M one-day move in PYUSD.
- [USDC Adds $76M Against The Week](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-15/): USDC added $76.19M in a day after its market cap fell $1.03B over seven days. msUSD widened to 1,150 bps below peg; the next marker is a $25M XAUT session.
- [pmUSD Narrows To 3,379 Bps](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-14/): pmUSD sits 3,379 bps below peg at $0.662, 164 bps tighter on the day, while the DEWS ALERT count fell to 4 from 10. A $165M USDC session would turn its daily reversal into rotation.
- [USD1 Net Burns $13.69M](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-13/): USD1 read -100 against its 30-day baseline on $13.69M of net burns, and the Bank Run Gauge fell to -24.9, below 9 October's -19.4. A print of -30 or lower would make flow stress the next lead candidate.
- [USDe Yield Flag Holds As Supply Slips](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-12-weekly/): USDe held the week's top yield flag at 5.03% APY as its market cap slid to $4.75B. USDC was the largest supply mover on five days, -$1.15B on a trailing basis. PSI stayed BEDROCK, 88.6 to 92.5.
- [AUSD Leads Three Flow Shifts](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-12/): AUSD's pressure score hit -98 and USD1's -82 on $6.84M of combined net burns, while the Bank Run Gauge fell to -13 from -3. A print at -15 or lower makes flow stress the next lead.
- [USDC's Burn Slows To $13.42M](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-11/): USDC is down $1.10B on the week, but the last day took only $13.42M while USDD net minted $199.43M. A Bank Run Gauge print of -15 or lower would shift the story to flow stress.
- [apxUSD Closes A 159-Hour Depeg](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-10/): apxUSD is back at peg after a 372 bps trough on $309.70M of supply, and its Safety Score is still F (31). USDC's $1.17B weekly contraction exceeds the whole market's $418M decline.
- [USDC Burns $455M In A Day](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-09/): USDC burned $455.28M in a day, 44% of a $1.04B weekly contraction, while total stablecoin supply is still up $366.60M on the week. A $570M single-day USDC print is the next line.
- [PSI Falls To A Tracking Low](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-08/): PSI reads 90.7, its lowest in 224 days of tracking, with total market cap 0.20% under its high. Breadth supplies 6.81 points of drag; depeg severity supplies 0.03.
- [USDT Adds $482.55M On The Week](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-07/): USDT supply rose $482.55M in seven days to $184.30B while USDC shed $141.55M in one. A USDC day of $180M or more would mark rotation rather than drift.
- [pmUSD Narrows On Split Feeds](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-06/): pmUSD sits at $0.474, 5,257 bps off peg and 122 bps better than yesterday, but DEWS scores its cross-source divergence at 100. PSI fell to 91, its lowest in 222 days of tracking.
- [apxUSD Clears 3,159 bps, Then Slips Again](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-05-weekly/): apxUSD ended a 3,159 bps depeg after 2,527 hours on 2026-09-30, then opened a 111 bps gap by 2026-10-03. USDC led supply declines on all seven days as total cap rose 0.81%.
- [EURC Burns $6.59M Net](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-05/): EURC net burns hit $6.59M in 24h, a -100 pressure reading, as the Bank Run Gauge fell from 4.1 to -14.5. reUSD minted $3.64M the other way.
- [USDf Adds $198.76M In A Day](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-04/): USDf posted $198.76M of net issuance in 24 hours, about an eighth of its $1.62B market cap, as the Bank Run Gauge reads 4.1 after six daily readings below -15.
- [USDC's Weekly Burn Slows](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-03/): USDC is down $1.20B on the week but removed only $53.75M in the latest day, while total stablecoin market cap reached $322.03B. Next trigger: apxUSD reaching 150 bps off peg, from 111 now.
- [USDC Shrinks, Market Cap Barely Moves](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-02/): USDC's supply fell $2.28B in seven days while total stablecoin market cap slipped only $443.5M; USDT and PYUSD added $399.76M between them in a single day.
- [USDe Net Burns Reach $36.75M](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-10-01/): USDe retired $36.75M net in 24 hours and the Bank Run Gauge fell to -23.6. apxUSD sits 108 bps below peg; 150 bps is the level that would make it a stronger peg-stress signal.
- [apxUSD Recovers, Grade Stays F](https://pharos.watch/digest/2026-09-30/): apxUSD's depeg closed after 2,527 hours and a 3,159 bps trough, yet its safety grade is still F at 30. USDC supply fell $1.35B in a week; next trigger is a $10M one-day USDe move.

## Stablecoins Index

- [Tether (USDT)](https://pharos.watch/stablecoin/usdt-tether/): centralized stablecoin backed by real-world assets pegged to US Dollar.
